I found three B2B SaaS founders under 5k followers whose posts took off in the past week (Sep 21–28). I ran about 20 Google `site:x.com` searches limited to the past week, then opened each post and profile on X to get exact numbers.

### 1. Omar Shaik (@omarshaik): 2,532 followers
- **What:** A single post on Sep 25 announcing that **Replit acquired Atta**, his AI analytics startup. It also tells the backstory: two years ago he cold-emailed Replit's CEO asking him to invest.
- **Numbers:** 286K views, 284 likes, 58 replies, 23 reposts.
- **Where his profile was at:** **A one-off blow-up.** His posts from the previous month got about 100–450 views and 0–3 likes each, so this was roughly 600x his usual reach. The news drove it, not a content habit.
- **Link:** https://x.com/omarshaik/status/2103515238243221725

### 2. Halfdan Timm (@halfdantimm): 2,770 followers
- **What:** A story post on Sep 26. A salesperson for a B2B SaaS wouldn't share the price without a meeting, so he **vibe-coded his own version of the tool** instead. It rides on a topic @levelsio has been posting about.
- **Numbers:** 113K views, 335 likes, 158 bookmarks, 34 replies.
- **Where his profile was at:** **Mostly a one-off, but not his first.** He posts rarely (about 2–4 times a month), and his normal posts get 400–800 views and 2–8 likes. He did have a smaller hit on Aug 9 (44K views, 137 likes). Caveat: he co-founded an agency (Obsidian Agency, sold to private equity twice), so he's not strictly a SaaS founder. The viral post is about B2B SaaS, though.
- **Link:** https://x.com/halfdantimm/status/2103923959481684000

### 3. Nick Velkovski (@nikolak47): 2,844 followers
- **What:** Two hits in the same week:
  - **An X article on Sep 22,** "Crush LinkedIn outreach with Jev," about building an outreach bot for LinkedIn. 30.7K views, 176 likes, 460 bookmarks (a lot of saves, so people found it useful).
  - **A long post on Sep 24** about hitting **$18M ARR at HeyReach** (bootstrapped, 7,500+ customers), with the good and the bad of getting there. 26K views, 151 likes. It's pinned on his profile.
- **Where his profile was at:** **Already on a streak, not a one-off.** His everyday posts already get 2–6K views, far more than you'd expect from 2.8k followers. He's the CEO of a real $18M ARR company who posts often, so his numbers keep climbing rather than jumping once.
- **Links:**
  - Article: https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2102457147498140050
  - ARR post: https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2103183053275431110

### Checked and ruled out (too many followers or not B2B SaaS)
- **Over 5k followers:** Rob Hoffman (14.8K, whose "About Us" page guide got 1.1M views), Alexa Belonix (25.8K), David Ch (18K), Rob Hallam (64K), Paul Mit (26K), Vincent Alonzi (23K), Alex Vacca (36K), Hasan Cagli (12.4K), Suraj Sharma (16.6K), Mubbu (166K).
- **VCs:** Martin Tobias.
- **Not B2B SaaS:** Sumukha Nadig (784 followers, but it's a funding announcement for a sleep and longevity startup).

**Limitations:** Google indexes only part of X, so this list isn't complete. There are almost certainly more underdog posts that Google hasn't picked up yet.

I found three B2B SaaS founders under 5k followers whose posts took off in the past week (Sep 21–28). I ran about 20 Google `site:x.com` searches limited to the past week, then opened each post and profile on X to get exact numbers.

### 1. Omar Shaik (@omarshaik): 2,532 followers
- **What:** A single post on Sep 25 announcing that **Replit acquired Atta**, his AI analytics startup. It also tells the backstory: two years ago he cold-emailed Replit's CEO asking him to invest.
- **Numbers:** 286K views, 284 likes, 58 replies, 23 reposts.
- **Where his profile was at:** **A one-off blow-up.** His posts from the previous month got about 100–450 views and 0–3 likes each, so this was roughly 600x his usual reach. The news drove it, not a content habit.
- **Link:** https://x.com/omarshaik/status/2103515238243221725

### 2. Halfdan Timm (@halfdantimm): 2,770 followers
- **What:** A story post on Sep 26. A salesperson for a B2B SaaS wouldn't share the price without a meeting, so he **vibe-coded his own version of the tool** instead. It rides on a topic @levelsio has been posting about.
- **Numbers:** 113K views, 335 likes, 158 bookmarks, 34 replies.
- **Where his profile was at:** **Mostly a one-off, but not his first.** He posts rarely (about 2–4 times a month), and his normal posts get 400–800 views and 2–8 likes. He did have a smaller hit on Aug 9 (44K views, 137 likes). Caveat: he co-founded an agency (Obsidian Agency, sold to private equity twice), so he's not strictly a SaaS founder. The viral post is about B2B SaaS, though.
- **Link:** https://x.com/halfdantimm/status/2103923959481684000

### 3. Nick Velkovski (@nikolak47): 2,844 followers
- **What:** Two hits in the same week:
  - **An X article on Sep 22,** "Crush LinkedIn outreach with Jev," about building an outreach bot for LinkedIn. 30.7K views, 176 likes, 460 bookmarks (a lot of saves, so people found it useful).
  - **A long post on Sep 24** about hitting **$18M ARR at HeyReach** (bootstrapped, 7,500+ customers), with the good and the bad of getting there. 26K views, 151 likes. It's pinned on his profile.
- **Where his profile was at:** **Already on a streak, not a one-off.** His everyday posts already get 2–6K views, far more than you'd expect from 2.8k followers. He's the CEO of a real $18M ARR company who posts often, so his numbers keep climbing rather than jumping once.
- **Links:**
  - Article: https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2102457147498140050
  - ARR post: https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2103183053275431110

### Checked and ruled out (too many followers or not B2B SaaS)
- **Over 5k followers:** Rob Hoffman (14.8K, whose "About Us" page guide got 1.1M views), Alexa Belonix (25.8K), David Ch (18K), Rob Hallam (64K), Paul Mit (26K), Vincent Alonzi (23K), Alex Vacca (36K), Hasan Cagli (12.4K), Suraj Sharma (16.6K), Mubbu (166K).
- **VCs:** Martin Tobias.
- **Not B2B SaaS:** Sumukha Nadig (784 followers, but it's a funding announcement for a sleep and longevity startup).

**Limitations:** Google indexes only part of X, so this list isn't complete. There are almost certainly more underdog posts that Google hasn't picked up yet.
